key_insight: AdaFuse adaptively fuses multiple LLMs at inference by changing fusion granularity mid-generation and applying test-time scaling to model logits, so ensembles combine complementary strengths per token without any retraining.
problem_solved: Fixed-granularity ensembling and uncalibrated voting fail to adapt to varying strengths across a generation and can be dominated by overconfident models; AdaFuse addresses the need for dynamic, calibrated ensemble decoding at test time.
method: Adaptive fusion granularity: dynamically decide fusion at token- or span-level (per-token gating/weighting) so the ensemble adapts mid-generation to which model is most reliable.
Test-time scaling of logits: apply model-specific scaling/calibration during inference to correct confidence imbalances and better balance contributions.
Integrated ensemble decoding: combine dynamic weights and scaled logits into standard decoding (greedy/beam/sampling) with minimal extra compute and no retraining required.
impact: Practitioners can improve generation quality, robustness, and controllability by combining off-the-shelf LLMs at inference time—no retraining—making ensemble gains practical for production and research.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: decoding loop showing per-token dynamic weighting and test-time scaling before token selection.
Heatmap: per-token/step model contribution weights across an example generation to illustrate mid-generation shifts.
Before/After calibration plot: logits or confidence distributions showing how test-time scaling reduces overconfidence.
Performance bar chart: comparison of AdaFuse vs fixed fusion baselines on key metrics (accuracy/ROUGE/win-rate) and latency overhead.
paper_title: AdaFuse: Adaptive Ensemble Decoding with Test-Time Scaling for LLMs
paper_authors: Chengming Cui, Tianxin Wei, Ziyi Chen, Ruizhong Qiu, Zhichen Zeng
